findings.trigger_condition: Processing a graph that contains both hashable and unhashable nodes, particularly dense graphs where hashable nodes are repeatedly looked up.
findings.root_cause: The `_id_of` function unconditionally scans `unhashable_ids` for every hashable node lookup (and `hashable_ids` for unhashable nodes), even when an exact match was already found in the primary registry. Assuming transitive equality, an item cannot exist independently in both registries if they are equal, rendering the secondary scan redundant for known nodes.
findings.impact: Severe performance degradation. Looking up a registered hashable node takes O(U) time instead of O(1), and an unhashable node takes O(U + H) instead of O(U), forcing unnecessary linear scans per edge. This degrades overall time complexity to O(E * U), which can be O(V^3) on dense mixed graphs.
findings.suggested_validation: Add an early return (`if match is not None: return match`) immediately after the first registry loop in both branches (hashable and unhashable) to bypass the secondary scan when a match is already confirmed.
